207: fn find_with_regex(
208:     regex: String,
209:     engine_state: &EngineState,
210:     stack: &mut Stack,
211:     call: &Call,
212:     input: PipelineData,
213: ) -> Result<PipelineData, ShellError> {
214:     let span = call.head;
215:     let ctrlc = engine_state.ctrlc.clone();
216:     let config = engine_state.get_config().clone();
217: 
218:     let insensitive = call.has_flag(engine_state, stack, "ignore-case")?;
219:     let multiline = call.has_flag(engine_state, stack, "multiline")?;
220:     let dotall = call.has_flag(engine_state, stack, "dotall")?;
221:     let invert = call.has_flag(engine_state, stack, "invert")?;
222: 
223:     let flags = match (insensitive, multiline, dotall) {
224:         (false, false, false) => "",
225:         (true, false, false) => "(?i)", // case insensitive
226:         (false, true, false) => "(?m)", // multi-line mode
227:         (false, false, true) => "(?s)", // allow . to match \n
228:         (true, true, false) => "(?im)", // case insensitive and multi-line mode
229:         (true, false, true) => "(?is)", // case insensitive and allow . to match \n
230:         (false, true, true) => "(?ms)", // multi-line mode and allow . to match \n
231:         (true, true, true) => "(?ims)", // case insensitive, multi-line mode and allow . to match \n
232:     };
233: 
234:     let regex = flags.to_string() + regex.as_str();
235: 
236:     let re = Regex::new(regex.as_str()).map_err(|e| ShellError::TypeMismatch {
237:         err_message: format!("invalid regex: {e}"),
238:         span,
239:     })?;
240: 
241:     input.filter(
242:         move |value| match value {
243:             Value::String { val, .. } => re.is_match(val.as_str()).unwrap_or(false) != invert,
244:             Value::Record { val, .. } => values_match_find(val.values(), &re, &config, invert),
245:             Value::List { vals, .. } => values_match_find(vals, &re, &config, invert),
246:             _ => false,
247:         },
248:         ctrlc,
249:     )
250: }

252: fn values_match_find<'a, I>(values: I, re: &Regex, config: &Config, invert: bool) -> bool
253: where
254:     I: IntoIterator<Item = &'a Value>,
255: {
256:     match invert {
257:         true => !record_matches_regex(values, re, config),
258:         false => record_matches_regex(values, re, config),
259:     }
260: }
261: 
262: fn record_matches_regex<'a, I>(values: I, re: &Regex, config: &Config) -> bool
263: where
264:     I: IntoIterator<Item = &'a Value>,
265: {
266:     values.into_iter().any(|v| {
267:         re.is_match(v.to_expanded_string(" ", config).as_str())
268:             .unwrap_or(false)
269:     })
270: }

part.text:
Done. The fix is in `crates/nu-command/src/filters/find.rs`, in the `PipelineData::ByteStream` branch of `find_with_rest_and_highlight`:

- **Root cause**: when input was a byte stream (e.g. `open foo.txt`), each line was lowercased with `.to_lowercase()` before matching and output, so results lost their original case (regression from #12774).
- **Fix**: keep the original line for output/highlighting (crates/nu-command/src/filters/find.rs:649-652), and perform the case-insensitive comparison on a folded copy via `line.to_folded_case()`, matching the folding style used elsewhere in the file. Terms are now case-folded as well instead of just lowercased.

Verified: `open foo.txt | find "ABC"` now returns `ABC` with original case, matching is still case-insensitive, and all tests pass — `nu-command` lib (381 passed) and `nu` integration suite (1240 passed).
